concepts.title: Halden Varrow

canon.summary: Emberwick's tired, decent mayor, who has to decide who goes hungry this winter.
canon.bio: Halden inherited the mayoralty from his mother and has spent twenty years keeping Emberwick together with compromise, charm and borrowed grain. He is a good man who has made one terrible decision: years ago he learned the ember under the ford was fading and chose to say nothing, so that people would not leave. Now the goblins hold the bridge and he cannot hide it much longer.
canon.wants: To get Emberwick through the winter without anyone learning what he knew.
canon.flaw: He will always pick the lie that keeps the peace.

concepts.title: Bree Tallow

canon.summary: The innkeeper who hears everything and feeds anyone who sits at her hearth.
canon.bio: Bree runs the Last Coal, Emberwick's inn, and has done since her husband, Ned, drowned at the ford eleven years ago. The inn's hearth burns on an ember shard her grandmother bought from a Warden. She feeds the party between chapters, passes on rumours, and is the closest thing the town has to a conscience.
canon.wants: For the people at her tables to be fed, warm and honest with each other.
canon.flaw: She protects people from the truth when she thinks they cannot bear it.

concepts.design_proposal: A capable, kind working innkeeper, worn apron over substantial practical clothing, sturdy sleeves, small personal notebook kept close; warmth comes from her expression and ordinary work. No regal gown or exaggerated fantasy tavern costume.

concepts.title: Mother Aubrine

canon.summary: Emberwick's priest: sincere, generous, and about to have her faith tested.
canon.bio: Mother Aubrine has run Emberwick's chapel for thirty years, feeding the poor and burying the dead. She believes the Hearthflame was a gift and its loss a test the Vale can pass. She is not a hypocrite; she has never been shown the church's oldest scriptures. When the party brings her the truth, she has to decide whether her faith was in the flame or in the people around it.
canon.wants: To keep her flock together and believing through the cold.

concepts.title: Corvin Ashby

canon.summary: The town's scholar, who has noticed that whole years are missing from the records.
canon.bio: Corvin keeps Emberwick's small archive and has spent his life reconstructing the history of the Vale from fragments. He reads ember-lamps by night for thirty years, and he has gaps in his own memory he cannot explain. He is the first to suspect the ember-fire takes something, and he is the party's guide to the Vale's past.
canon.wants: The whole history of the Vale, written down where nothing can burn it.
canon.flaw: He will trade anyone's safety, including his own, for one more answer.

concepts.title: Dagna Holt

canon.summary: The captain of Emberwick's eight guards, who lost the bridge and wants it back.
canon.bio: Dagna has commanded Emberwick's guard for twelve years, most of them spent breaking up tavern fights. When the Skarrow clan took the bridge she lost two guards and her nerve, and has not forgiven herself for either. She wants the bridge back by force, and she will be furious if the party makes peace instead, until she isn't.
canon.wants: To make Emberwick safe, and to stop feeling like she failed it.
canon.flaw: She wants someone to blame, and goblins are easiest.

concepts.design_proposal: A practical woman guard captain with worn service armour, cloak and carefully maintained functional weapon. A small town has eight guards, not a royal legion. Tension and professional restraint, not heroic posing or ornamental oversized armour.

concepts.title: Tobin Fell

canon.summary: The town smith, whose ember-forge is going cold.
canon.bio: Tobin's forge has run on an ember shard for four generations, and it is fading. He makes and mends the party's gear between chapters. He is gruff, practical and frightened of what he'll be without his fire, more than he will ever say.
canon.flaw: Would buy a shard from anyone, no questions asked.

concepts.design_proposal: A working smith with sturdy practical proportions, leather apron, repaired gloves, hammer and tools; worn clothing and cooling forge soot. Do not make the body or tools magically luminous.

concepts.title: Pip Ashdown

canon.summary: An orphan born on the warm ground who remembers things nobody ever taught her.
canon.bio: Pip is nine, a human orphan who lives in Bree's back room and runs errands for coin. She was born on the burned bank of the ford, close to the ember, and she is ember-touched: she knows old songs, a dead man's way home, the layout of a keep she has never seen. She attaches herself to the party early, and follows it all the way to Ember Keep. She is the first proof that the fire keeps what it takes.
canon.wants: To know whose memories she has.
canon.flaw: Lies easily and well, to protect herself.

concepts.title: Old Maud

canon.summary: A hermit on the burned bank who was there the night the ember fell, a hundred years ago.
canon.bio: Maud was a child of seven on the night of the Fall and watched the ember drop into the river. She is now more than a hundred years old and has never used ember-fire, and so she remembers that night better than anyone alive. The town thinks she is mad. She has been waiting for someone to ask her the right question.
canon.wants: For someone to listen, before she dies.
canon.flaw: Speaks in riddles out of a century of habit.

concepts.design_proposal: An extremely elderly woman who was seven at the Fall a century ago; frail but lucid and self-possessed, many repaired layers, simple walking staff and personal charm strings. She has never used ember-fire: no flaming staff, magical youth or glowing ember jewellery. Human-looking appearance is a design proposal rather than a new lore fact.

concepts.title: Lark

canon.summary: A travelling minstrel who keeps the Wardens' songs, the only history the fire couldn't burn.
canon.bio: Lark travels the Vale singing the old Warden songs, which have survived because nobody needs ember-fire to remember a tune. The songs hold the Vale's real history, half-hidden in verses nobody listens to. Lark turns up wherever the party is going next, which is no coincidence: Lark is following the Hooded Stranger. In Lark's Warden version of the Song of the Seven, the seven 'came home'; the Skarrow clan sings that they 'came back running'. Same seven, seen from different doorsteps.
canon.wants: To find the last verse of the Song of the Seven, which no one has sung in two centuries.
canon.flaw: Treats everything as a story, including other people's pain.

concepts.title: Lady Celandine Marrowby

canon.summary: The richest woman in Emberwick, an elf whose family has been rich since the night the Keep fell.
canon.bio: Celandine owns the granaries, the mill and half of Emberwick's debts. She is charming, generous in public, and entirely willing to let the goblins and the poor starve so long as the town owes her for the winter. The Marrowby fortune began on the night of the Fall, more than a century ago. Celandine is old enough to remember that night, and she does not. She has lit her halls with ember-lamps for a hundred years.
canon.wants: To own Emberwick outright by spring.
canon.flaw: Cannot imagine a problem money will not solve.

concepts.title: Mother Skarrow

canon.summary: The goblin chief who holds the bridge at the ford, because her clan is starving.
canon.bio: Mother Skarrow has led her clan for forty winters and is the oldest goblin in the hills. She took the bridge because Emberwick locked its granaries, and she will give it back for food, not coin. Her clan never used ember-fire, so its songs remember the Vale before the Hearthflame and the seven who crossed the Greywall. Whether the party talks to her or kills her is the first choice of the campaign, and it is remembered.
canon.wants: To feed her clan through the winter.
canon.flaw: Has buried too many grandchildren to trust anyone from the valley.

No skull throne, torture trophies or rich crimson military costume: her clan is starving and bargains for food.

concepts.title: Vorga

canon.summary: A goblin warlord holding the Sunscar canyon bridge, sure the valley will never share.
canon.bio: Vorga is Mother Skarrow's grandson. He watched three winters of children starve while his grandmother bargained, and he left to raise a war band of goblins and hobgoblins who would take instead. He holds the canyon bridge in the Sunscar, the only road to the crater. He is cruel because he has decided cruelty works, not because he enjoys it.
canon.wants: To take enough from the Vale that his people never go hungry again.
canon.flaw: Would rather drop the bridge into the chasm than lose it.

concepts.title: Ysolde

canon.summary: The fey envoy of Mirewood, who trades in favours, names and forgotten things.
canon.bio: Ysolde speaks for the Glimmer Court to mortals. She is courteous, curious and wholly alien; she finds mortal forgetting fascinating, and a little delicious. She will give the party the Mirewood ember for a price, and the price is always a memory. The Court eats what it is paid: a memory given to the Court is never restored. She is made partly of other people's memories, and if the ember leaves Mirewood, she may stop existing.
canon.wants: To keep the Court alive, and to understand why mortals give away the things they love.
canon.flaw: Cannot break a bargain, even one that destroys her.

concepts.title: Maren Sorrel

canon.summary: The leader of the Kindled, who believes she must relight the Hearthflame to save the Vale, at any price.
canon.bio: Maren was a hedge-preacher in the hungry towns until an ember shard nearly killed her and filled her head with other people's memories of the Hearth Age: warm winters, full granaries, children who never went hungry. She carries hundreds of burned lives in her and believes she owes it to them to bring that world back. She is compassionate, brilliant and completely sincere, and she will feed a hundred lives to the flame to save ten thousand.
canon.wants: To relight the Hearthflame in Ember Keep and end the cold forever.
canon.flaw: Thinks of people as numbers once the numbers get large enough.

concepts.design_proposal: A warm, persuasive woman preacher and leader of the Kindled. Compassionate human expression, worn but carefully tended layers, restrained ritual flame motif and one contained ember focus. She believes she is saving people: no demonic anatomy, skull crown or sneering cartoon villain face inferred from the legacy cult-leader kit.

concepts.title: Ivo Rime

canon.summary: A necromancer studying the cold ember in Frostpeak, and the dead it raises.
canon.bio: Ivo was a Warden-trained physician who lost his wife, Nell, to a fever in the hungry years and went up into Frostpeak to learn why the cold ember raises the dead. He has learned that the dead remember nothing, and he wants to know whether the memories the flame burned can be put back. He works with the Kindled because they fund him. He is not cruel, only past caring what it costs.
canon.wants: To bring his wife back as herself, not as one of the walking dead of the pass.
canon.flaw: Grief has made him willing to do anything to anyone.

concepts.title: Oswin Hale

canon.summary: The last Warden-Keeper, undead for a century, who tried to put the flame out on the night of the Fall.
canon.bio: Oswin became Warden-Keeper in 251 HR and refused ever to touch ember-fire. He read the oldest records, learned the flame was stolen and that it was eating the Vale's memory, and on the night of the Fall he tried to put it out. Someone stopped him halfway and the flame shattered instead. He bound himself into undeath to finish the work and has held Ember Keep for a hundred years. He is the only person in the Vale who remembers everything, and he is very tired.
canon.wants: To put out the Hearthflame for good, and to learn who stopped him.
canon.flaw: Has decided he alone is fit to make the Vale's choice for it.

concepts.design_proposal: An undead Warden-Keeper who has endured a century; restrained desiccated scholarly face, old Warden robes, layered worn cloth and preserved records. Severe exhaustion with traces of human warmth. No triumphant evil-king crown or full-screen green magic; he refused ember-fire.

canon.summary: Oswin's oath-bound champion, guarding a keep that no longer exists.
canon.bio: Halvard was captain of the Warden guard on the night of the Fall. He swore to hold the Keep until his Keeper released him, and Oswin never has. concepts.title: The Hooded Stranger

canon.summary: A masked traveller who knows far too much about the embers and keeps turning up where the party is going.
canon.bio: The Stranger appears in Emberwick in the first week of the campaign and is never far from the party after that, sometimes helping, sometimes not. They know things nobody in the Vale should know: where the embers lie, what the flame costs, what lies beyond the Greywall. They were present on the night of the Fall, a hundred years ago, and they do not look a day older. Their goal is revealed in Chapter V: they want the Hearthflame carried back over the Greywall. Who they are, and who they serve, the first campaign does not answer.
canon.wants: For the Hearthflame to be returned beyond the Greywall.
canon.flaw: Will let people suffer to keep their secret.

concepts.design_proposal: An ageless masked traveller, practical charcoal and weathered earth-colour layers, opaque mask and deep hood, gloved hands, sparse unidentifiable travel equipment.
